pathology.title: Right extensor digiti minimi · Injury & disease · draft
pathology.body: Extensor tendon injury can impair finger straightening. Superficial tendons on the back of the hand are vulnerable to cuts.
bullets: The level matters: terminal tendon injury may cause mallet finger, while central-slip injury can produce a different joint pattern.

xray.title: Right radial artery · Plain-film arterial calcification orientation · draft
xray.body: Yang and colleagues compared plain radiographs and ultrasound of bilateral radial and ulnar arteries in 40 adults receiving stable haemodialysis with forearm fistulas. A calcified wall may project along the radial arterial course; this is an indirect mineralisation sign, not a visible normal arterial lumen.
bullets: Keep the selected radial artery separate from the ulnar artery and its smaller neighbours. Projection and overlap do not establish a continuous arterial tree.
The study used posterior-anterior and lateral radiographs in a selected renal cohort. Its findings are not a healthy-population detection rate, and a negative film does not exclude vascular disease.
Plain-film calcification alone cannot measure flow, establish patency or grade stenosis. The reference mesh supplies none of these findings and is not the study participant’s artery.

Do not transfer these findings to radial branches or perforators. Published diagnostic-performance percentages are deliberately omitted because the displayed contingency table and reported denominators are inconsistent.

ultrasound.title: Interosseous membrane of left forearm · Ultrasound: distinguish the membrane from its model · draft
ultrasound.body: Ultrasound can assess the forearm interosseous membrane between the two bones. A controlled cadaver study compared ultrasound and MRI after complete experimental disruption of the central membrane; this is narrower evidence than detecting every clinical injury.
bullets: Do not transfer results from a deliberately cut central segment to partial, peripheral or chronic tears, or assume one normal image clears the entire membrane.

The displayed surface has no probe orientation, acoustic response or real-time tissue movement. Its continuity cannot demonstrate a normal patient membrane or exclude associated elbow and wrist injury.

pathology.title: Interosseous membrane of left forearm · Injury & disease · draft
pathology.body: An Essex–Lopresti injury combines a radial-head fracture, forearm interosseous-membrane disruption and distal radioulnar joint injury. Together these can produce longitudinal forearm instability; an isolated radial-head fracture does not by itself establish this combined injury.
bullets: Elbow and wrist findings can belong to the same forearm injury rather than two unrelated problems.
A whole membrane surface cannot show which band has failed or quantify displacement under load.
One indexed membrane surface per side; individual bands and insertions are not separately segmented. No patient-specific stability, injury grade or biomechanical simulation.

bullets: Clinical examination and appropriate imaging determine the injury pattern; an assembled reference atlas does not exclude disruption.

pathology.title: Right radial recurrent artery · A distal pulse does not exclude arterial injury · draft

bullets: A radial pulse is not a direct test of this particular recurrent branch. No pulse, Doppler signal or angiographic filling is generated by selecting it.

ultrasound.title: Right anterior ulnar recurrent artery · ultrasound evidence orientation · draft
ultrasound.body: Wei and colleagues reported 29 proximal ulnar perforator flaps in 25 patients, using high-frequency colour ultrasound to locate perforators before flap design. Their separate anatomical study described proximal forearm perforators from the ulnar and anterior ulnar recurrent arteries. These observations do not provide a detection rate for ultrasound visualization of the whole anterior recurrent parent artery.
bullets: Keep the anterior and posterior ulnar recurrent selections distinct. A proximal forearm perforator signal alone does not identify its parent branch.

pathology.title: Right anterior ulnar recurrent artery · An apparent alternative route may also be injured · draft
pathology.body: The anterior recurrent–inferior collateral pathway should not be treated as a guaranteed bypass around elbow injury. Damage can involve both the main brachial route and its surrounding network. The clinical question is which pathways actually remain intact, not how many branches are displayed.
bullets: Hiding the brachial artery does not test compensation. This view has no perfusion calculation, injury grading or reconstructed postoperative circulation.
